label: SET 6 Question Mismatch
centralQuestion: Does achieving 53% accuracy in decision-making really mean exceptional ability?

sources.title: Decision Accuracy in Investing
sources.summary: Discusses hit rates in stock picking and portfolio decisions.
sources.thesis: Professional investors are right only about half the time.
sources.centralQuestion: Professional investors are right only about half the time.

claims.statement: Professional stock pickers are right about fifty-three percent of the time on major directional calls.
claims.evidenceSummary: In professional stock picking you are right about fifty-three percent of the time on major directional calls. That hit rate is far from perfect but still beats random selection when position sizing is disciplined.

conclusions: Professional investors are right only about half the time.

sources.title: Failure and Personal Strength
sources.summary: Talks about failure, adaptation, and finding personal strengths.
sources.thesis: Failure is inevitable; success comes from adapting and finding what you are good at.
sources.centralQuestion: Failure is inevitable; success comes from adapting and finding what you are good at.

claims.statement: Success after failure depends on adapting and finding what you are uniquely good at.
claims.evidenceSummary: People experience failure repeatedly in competitive arenas. The key is not avoiding failure but adapting quickly and finding the specific capability you are uniquely good at.

conclusions: Failure is inevitable; success comes from adapting and finding what you are good at.

sources.title: Brand Values in Marketing
